row.name: Don't Climb That She Said
row.overview: A short, easy-to-miss V0+ boulder problem on a flat-topped erratic beside the White Chuck Glacier basin, climbed almost in passing by parties on Glacier Peak's standard south-side approach.
row.beta: A single Gaston move with the left hand plus careful footwork gets you to the flat summit in one or two moves.
row.comms: No cell coverage on the approach trail.
row.descent: Downclimb or step off; not a roped route.

waypoints.name: Don't Climb That She Said boulder

sectionBreakdown.note: The 0.6 mi and 2 hr here describe the boulder session itself, not the journey to it. This problem sits roughly 8 miles up the North Fork Sauk approach trail toward Glacier Peak, so reaching it is a multi-day wilderness trip requiring a self-issue wilderness permit — do not read these figures as a car-to-car outing.
sectionBreakdown.fromTo: Boulder session on the Glacier Peak approach

row.detailed_rack: None — boulder problem, no gear required (optional crash pad).
pro_tips: There's a small flat spot for a single tent directly at the base of the boulder — a novelty high-camp option
Usually climbed incidentally by parties passing through on the standard south-side approach, not as a dedicated objective
watch_out: This is not a route to Glacier Peak's summit — don't confuse it with the mountain's actual climbing routes.
row.best_season: Summer (Jul-Sep) — the approach requires snow-free high-alpine trail conditions.
row.approach: Reach it by the North Fork Sauk River trail, the standard southern approach to Glacier Peak: past Mackinaw Shelter, up the long switchbacks to the Pacific Crest Trail at White Pass, then east on the climbers' path toward the White Chuck Glacier basin. The boulder stands west of what is left of the White Chuck Glacier, in view of the path, and is easy to recognise by its flat top; there is room for a single tent at its foot.
row.descent_text: This is a boulder problem (0 pitches, no rope-length or anchor data of any kind), so there is no rappelling involved — descent is a walk-off / down-climb back to the base along the same short use-trail used on the approach, then out the way you came to the trailhead. Land on pads, spot as usual for the topout, and watch footing on any wet rock or duff on the way down.

pitch_detail.notes: Gaston left hand, careful footwork, one to two moves to a flat top.

access.fees: None beyond the parking or entrance fee this route already lists.
access.rules: Group size capped at 12 (people + stock combined) in Glacier Peak Wilderness; larger groups must split with 1-mile separation. Campfires prohibited above 3,500 ft.
access.seasonal: Mountain Loop Highway has a seasonal gate closure (Deer Creek–Bedal, ~14 mi), typically Nov–mid/late May. Suiattle River Road (FSR 26), the primary Glacier Peak access, has had storm-damage closures — check current conditions before a trip.
